title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-FAIRROUND-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-FAIRROUND-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `818fe7861`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-FAIRROUND-1

## Summary

Ported the teammate-delivered `fair-round-20261108` fix for responder starvation
in `runTeammateResponder` (`src/core/comms/imessage-teammate-worker.ts`).

Bug: the scan was `inbox.texts.slice(0, 256)` over an `at`-ordered (record-time)
inbox. A text that is re-recorded late — e.g. `recordTeammateText` failing in
`ingestIMessages` (`deferred` break, cursor not advanced, re-ingested next poll
with a fresh `at`) — lands at the tail of the at-order, behind every newer
text. Under sustained arrival pressure beyond 256 unanswered rows, the old
receipt stays outside the bounded window forever; new replyable messages
indefinitely defer it.

Fix (fair scan rounds): the responder now freezes a per-round upper rowid
(`scanCeiling`) in the receipt store and sweeps the frozen range in rowid order,
tracked by a persisted cursor (`scanAfter`), across as many passes as the
per-pass bounds (256 examined, 3 work items) take. Eligibility is by rowid —
the stable arrival order — so an `at`-late straggler keeps its arrival rank.
Arrivals past the frozen bound wait for the next round: a bounded deferral,
never starvation. The round completes by coverage (every in-range text visited
once), so permanently-pending texts (unapproved/leader) cannot deadlock it;
they are re-swept in the following round as before. Budget-breakers restore
the pre-message checkpoint so they keep their existing retry-next-pass cadence.
Sibling precedent: `imessage-findings-bridge.ts` already re-sorts `texts` by
rowid for its watermark scan for the same `at`-inversion reason.

Files changed (all left uncommitted for publish.sh):

- `src/core/comms/imessage-teammate-worker.ts` (+24/-5):
  `Store` gains optional `scanAfter`/`scanCeiling` (schema-validated when
  present); the loop head becomes the round open/sweep; the two
  `processed >= 3` breaks restore the checkpoint; post-loop persists
  `scanAfter` and clears `scanCeiling` when the sweep reaches `rangeEnd`.
- `test/imessage-teammate-worker.test.ts` (+24/-1): two regression tests —
  an `at`-inverted old receipt behind 261 newer texts is replied to, and a
  post-ceiling arrival is held exactly one round then processed — plus the
  `senderIdFor` import.

## Patch provenance / deviation note

`~/.ashlr-runs/imessage/patches/patch-fair-round-20261108.RAW.diff` is not
readable from this worktree sandbox (`~/.ashlr-runs` is seatbelt-denied for the
agent process; `request_scope` grant, the `read` tool, `osascript`, `mdfind`,
the `gh` CLI config, MCP servers, and the hub API all failed or lacked access).
The fix was therefore reconstructed manually from the job description
("freezes a scan-round upper rowid so new arrivals cannot indefinitely defer
old receipts", superseding the withdrawn fair-scan candidate) and verified
against the starvation mechanism in the current source. If a reviewer diffs
against the RAW artifact, expect different line shapes for the same semantics.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/imessage-teammate-worker.test.ts` —
  16/16 PASS (2 new + 14 existing).
- Same file re-run with `HEAD` worker restored: the 2 new tests FAIL (14
  pass) — confirms they pin the fixed behavior. New code re-restored after.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (once,
  foreground): file selection PASS, `tsc --noEmit` PASS, web typecheck
  skipped (no `src/web-ui` change), realio lane lint PASS, verse sync-I/O lint
  PASS. eslint SKIP: `node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js` absent in this worktree
  (no `npm ci` run); Merge Gate lints on CI.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` — PASS (`errors: []`).

## Pass/fail counts

- Tests: 16 pass, 0 fail.
- verify-changed: all applicable phases PASS; eslint skipped (no node_modules).
- check:docs: 0 errors.

## Net LOC

`git diff --stat`: 2 files, +48/-6 (net +42).

## Limitations

- Literal patch artifact unreadable under this sandbox; the port is a
  semantics-faithful reconstruction (see provenance note).
- eslint not run locally (no `node_modules`); relies on Merge Gate lint.
- No commit/push performed; changes staged only in the worktree for
  publish.sh.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-REDIRECT-FIX-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-REDIRECT-FIX-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `818fe7861`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-REDIRECT-FIX-1

REWORKS_PR: 4088

## Summary

Security fix for PR #4088 (FIXUP-CI-phantom-ci local-bench transport), against
reviewed helper blob `48d16febab1378f4db5b5ad601b81430eda7ec55` (the worktree's
`src/core/radar/local-bench.ts` at HEAD — verified byte-identical via
`git hash-object`).

**Bug:** the bench validates that its base URL is loopback before any fetch,
but `chatCompletion` used the fetch default `redirect: 'follow'`. A validated
loopback endpoint answering 307/308 had undici re-POST the synthetic bench
body (instruction + fixture input) to whatever origin `Location` named — a
second hop nothing re-validated. The "loopback-only" guarantee therefore
leaked the request body to an arbitrary origin.

**Fix:** `redirect: 'error'` on the transport's fetch init — the same option
every other security-sensitive transport in this tree already uses
(`telemetry-sink.ts` "Never forward the credential to a redirect target",
`provider-client.ts`, `local-inference-probe.ts`, `ollama-identity.ts`,
`model-manager.ts`, …). Any redirect reply now fails the call; `scoreSuite`
records it as a `transport` error, the existing failure path. A legitimate
local model server never redirects `/v1/chat/completions`.

Module header "THE ONE RULE" and the emitted report `notes[]` now state the
redirect refusal so the documented invariant matches the code.

## Changes

- `src/core/radar/local-bench.ts` (+7/−2): `redirect: 'error'` in
  `chatCompletion`; header + report-notes wording.
- `test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts` (new, 78 lines, **real-io lane**):
  two real loopback HTTP servers — the first replies 301/302/303/307/308 with
  `Location` pointing at the second. Asserts the case is scored
  `error: 'transport'`, `answered: null`, and that the second listener saw
  **zero requests and zero body bytes**. Registered in
  `test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs` per the lane guard.
- `test/radar-local-bench.test.ts` (+20, unit lane): pins the transport
  contract — every `fetchImpl` call carries `redirect: 'error'`.
- `test/fixtures/radar-local-bench/README.md` (+3/−2): offline-test command
  names both suites; security-model line mentions redirect refusal.

## Commands run

```
# Affected tests (hermetic runner, temp HOME)
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/radar-local-bench.test.ts test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts
# → 2 files passed |unit| + |real-io|, 23 tests passed, 0 failed

# Regression proof: fix reverted, new suite must fail
git stash -- src/core/radar/local-bench.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts
# → 5/5 FAILED without the fix (body reached second listener; case scored as answered)
git stash pop

# Repo verification (AGENTS.md: automated workers run once, foreground)
HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs --force
# → PASS file selection / tsc --noEmit / realio lane lint / verse sync-I/O / verify dedupe
# → SKIP eslint: node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js absent in this worktree's
#   partial install (Merge Gate lints on CI)

# Docs check
npm run check:docs
# → PASS, errors: []

# Registry/drift suites touched by the new test file
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/authority-codeowners-310b.test.ts test/realio-lane-guard-green.test.ts test/doc-facts.test.ts
# → authority-codeowners PASS, doc-facts PASS
# → realio-lane-guard-green FAIL — pre-existing base-branch drift: it flags
#   test/ecosystem-changelog-generator.test.ts and
#   test/verse-standby-python-contract-02somp1.test.ts, both UNCHANGED here.
#   Not caused by this diff (verify-changed's changed-files scope: PASS).
```

## Pass/fail counts

- `test/radar-local-bench.test.ts`: 18/18 pass (was 17 before)
- `test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts`: 5/5 pass (301, 302, 303, 307, 308)
- Regression confirmed: all 5 fail without the fix
- verify-changed: all PASS (eslint skipped — see above)
- check:docs: PASS
- 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change: `realio-lane-guard-green`
  (flags two files untouched by this diff)

## Net LOC

Tracked: +31/−4 across 4 files; new file `test/radar-local-bench-redirect.test.ts`
+78. **Net +109/−4** (net +105 lines). No changes committed.

## Notes

- Boundary respected: no `git commit`/`push`, no `gh` writes — publish.sh owns
  publishing. All changes uncommitted in the worktree.
- Only `chatCompletion` performs network I/O in this module; no other fetch in
  the bench needed the option.
- Chose `redirect: 'error'` over `manual` + re-validation: the codebase's
  established convention for credential/body-bearing transports, and any
  redirect here is already a transport failure — there is no legitimate
  redirect target to re-validate for.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-DEPGATEQ8

Added `ashlr fleet dep-gate` — a read-only launch gate over the router queue.
For each non-PARKED row in `queue/ready.tsv` it reads the row's prompt file;
when the prompt declares `DEPENDENCY GATE: <ids>`, every id must have a
`{event:"outcome", state:"MERGED", job:<id>}` row in `metrics/jobs.jsonl`.
Each unmet id is listed as `UNMET-DEP <job> (<lane>): <ids>` (plain) or in the
`unmet` array (`--json`); exit is 1 when any unmet id is found or a source is
degraded, 2 on bad arguments. Root resolution is `--runs-dir`, then
`ASHLR_RUNS_DIR`, then `~/.ashlr-runs`, matching the fleet convention.

This complements `fleet parked`'s `unmetDeps` projection: parked rows are
expected to wait on their gate ids; `dep-gate` covers the rows still queued to
launch. Both ready.tsv layouts are handled — the dispatcher layout
(`job, repo, lane, tier, prompt`, prompt column 5) and the status-first layout
(`status, job, lane, tier, repo, prompt`, prompt column 6); either a status or
lane cell starting with `PARKED` skips the row. Prompt paths must resolve
inside the runs dir and are read bounded (64 KiB, `O_NOFOLLOW`) through the
shared `readSource`; `ready.tsv` (2 MiB head) and `jobs.jsonl` (2 MiB tail) get

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-COMMS-DEPTH-1 (unified comms inbox)

## Summary

`phm comms inbox [--json]` is now a read-only, prioritized roll-up of every
pending comms item, aggregating four local sources into one ranked list whose
items carry `act` deep-link commands:

- **needs-you** — unresolved `NEEDS-MASON.md` lines → `phm fleet needs-resolve <id> --reply "<reply>"`
- **imessage** — unanswered allowlisted teammate texts → `phm fleet teammate-texts --answered <rowid>` / `phm fleet bus-claim acquire --id imessage-teammate-<rowid> …`
- **drafts** — outbound drafts awaiting approval → `phm drafts show|approve|reject <id>`
- **bus** — live `kind:"work"` envelopes with no live claim (expired lease = unclaimed again) → `phm fleet bus-claim acquire --id <id> …`

Ranking reuses the Needs-you contract (`compareRanked` +
`needsYouPriorityHeuristic` in `src/core/decide/needs-you.ts`): severity band,
then priority (`now`/`today`/`this-week`/`whenever`), then expiry, then newest.
Deterministic, no model call, never mutates. Per-source `sources.<name>.state`
reports `healthy`/`missing`/`degraded`/`unavailable` so a broken store is never
read as "nothing pending"; output caps at 200 items with `omitted` counting the
remainder. Titles/details are secret-scrubbed and single-lined; claim tokens and
lease internals stay inside `bus-work-claims.ts` (new public
`inspectBusWorkClaims` view returns only id/cursor/receivedAt/owner/leaseUntil/
completedAt). Bare `inbox` prints a human view; `inbox --json` prints the report;
`inbox read|post` keep their original meaning.

To let the aggregator classify teammate texts without pulling the responder's
transport/model graph, the pure `teammateNeedsReply`/`classifyTeammateIntent`
regexes moved to the leaf module `imessage-teammate-inbox.ts`; the worker

  (deterministic `Revert "title"`/`Revert #N` > overlapping fix-file follow-up;
  ledger rows keyed by mergeCommit), `stable` requires the 72 h window elapsed
  AND the merge's own row in a covering gh export, otherwise `pending` /
  `unobserved`. Rates resolve over stable+adverse only; `ranked` sorts on the
  Wilson lower bound; CI block reports raw adverse rates by check state and
  job-finish failure plus a direction — never a significance claim.
- `src/cli/fleet-eval-report.ts` (new, 165 LOC): thin adapter — bounded file
  reads (16 MiB cap, ≤8 `--prs` files), `--jobs/--prs/--days/--until/
  --no-observations/--json`, dep injection for tests, exit 2 on bad args,
  exit 1 when no input source is readable.
- Registry regenerated (`'eval-report'` loader), `eval-report` added to fleet
  completions, docs in AGENTS.md + `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md`.

## Design notes / honesty stance

- Ledger-only merges (repo covered by export, PR absent from it) still earn
  deterministic revert detection via `Revert #N` refs, but are never `stable`.
- Merges with pending (non-concluded) checks report `checkState: unknown`,
  not `clean`.
- Publish/outcome rows without lane/tier borrow the producing job's latest
  routing row; attribution resolves post-fold so out-of-order rows still join.
- `ttm_s` prefers the ledger value; `mergeLead` falls back to mergedAt minus
  the job's first routing timestamp.
- Bodies/titles are parsed only for evidence matching — never echoed into the
  report.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-WTJANITOR-1 (fleet wt-audit)

## Summary

Adds `phm fleet wt-audit` — a read-only audit of the job-worktree root
(`~/Projects/ashlrai/wt`, ~912 dirs on the host) — plus a `--reap-plan`
mode that lists only worktrees the existing sanctioned reapers could
already take. The command deletes nothing, publishes nothing and writes
no queue state.

- `src/core/fleet/wt-audit.ts` (new, 722 LOC): injected-reader audit core.
  - Pure parsers: attempt-aware `jobs.jsonl` ledger (a `launch` resets
    terminal evidence of the previous attempt; `rows` never resets, so it
    stays the orphan detector), `mergedUrlsFromLedger` (dispatchd's
    `_merged_urls` shape), `.publish` RESULT classifier matching
    `reap-one.sh`'s case statement, `ps` scan (reap-one.sh/publish.sh
    children = in-flight; launch.sh/worktree/prompt paths = alive, with
    dispatchd.py self-rows filtered), status.json kept/reaping lists, and
    `queue/keep.txt`.
  - `classifyEntry` rolls evidence into one state per worktree:
    invalid / excluded (hidden + `guardian-*`) / running (`.dispatched`,
    `.pid`, live process, or named anywhere in status.json — reap-one's
    quiet check) / reaping / publishing / held (keep.txt, status
    `kept_worktrees`, `~/.ashlr/kept-worktrees.json` pins, RESULT
    DENIED/ABORT/secret-shape/other) / archived (RESULT ARCHIVED — needs
    the archive path's salvage verification) / merged / open / ended /
    published / empty / finished / recorded / orphaned / unknown.
  - Reap eligibility: `via: 'reap-one'` (job `.base` + terminal evidence;
    reap-one.sh runs publish.sh then removes) or `'worktree-remove'`
    (merged outcome, or published/empty without the `.base` the reaper
    needs — the removal `fleet worktree-stale --apply` / `wt-reap --apply`
    already performs). `reapable` only when `via` survives every gate.
  - Fail-closed gates strip `via` from every candidate when any safety
    source is unread: jobs ledger, status.json, process table, pin file,
    runs-dir listing (can't see `.base`/`.publish`), keep.txt, or the
    `queue/run` listing (can't see markers). `presence` distinguishes a
    positively-absent file (empty evidence, healthy) from a present-but-
    unreadable one (degraded). A 180 s evidence-freshness grace mirrors
    dispatchd's launch grace. Orphan is claimed only when every source is
    readable and still shows no evidence.
  - Sizes via the shared `measureWorktreeBytes` under one 20 s budget;
    bounded reads refuse symlinks (`O_NOFOLLOW`) and cap files at 256 KB /
    ledger at 8 MB.
- `src/cli/fleet-wt-audit.ts` (new, 84 LOC): thin dispatcher —
  `--json` (sanitized via `sanitizePublicJson`, home paths shown as `~`),
  `--reap-plan`, `--no-size`, `--wt-dir`, `--runs-dir`;
  `ASHLR_WT_DIR`/`ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` env like `fleet kept-age`.
  Exit 0 ok, 1 when the worktree root can't be listed, 2 bad usage.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (+1 generated line, `wt-audit`).
- `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md` (+1 table row, per the file's sync convention).
- `test/fleet-wt-audit.test.ts` (new, 452 LOC, 27 tests): fully hermetic —
  injected fs/ledger/ps/pins/measurer, temp HOME; covers attempt reset,
  publish classes, ps/status/keep parsing, every protected state, degraded
  fail-closed gates, freshness grace, realpath `.base` aliases, CLI exits.

## Safety properties

- Read-only: no deletes, no publishes, no marker or queue writes. The plan
  is a candidate list for the sanctioned tools (reap-one.sh, worktree
  removal), never an executor — same posture as `fleet reap-marks`.
- Never plans: running, reaping, publishing, held, archived, fresh,
  non-terminal, evidence-less, or any worktree while a safety source is
  unread. A `.base` only counts when its recorded worktree path resolves
  to this dir (realpath-checked), so a reused job id inherits nothing.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-CI-CANDIDATE-1

## Summary

Merge-evaluated the teammate's CI test candidate (described at master `6778b16`
as: quota custody preserving Darwin/APFS positive coverage + adding Linux
fail-closed, volume polling against the real storage checker, staging-stop
asserting both settled and unattempted reports). The candidate artifact itself
is not fetchable locally — `6778b16` is an unrelated worktree-heal commit, no
branch or PR ref containing it survives in this clone, and `gh` is blocked in
this sandbox — so the described semantics were reconstructed faithfully against
current HEAD, keeping only pieces still applicable.

## Ported

1. **Quota custody — own-pid self-clock verification**
   `src/core/resources/quota-refresh-lease.ts`: `observedOwnerStart` now uses
   `currentProcessStartIdentity()` when `lock.pid === process.pid`, keeping
   `verifiedProcessStartIdentity` (kernel probe) for foreign owners. This
   mirrors the established `hasVerifiedLiveOwner` convention in
   `src/core/fleet/local-store-lock.ts` ("the writer's immutable start
   identity… other owners still require a native probe"). Security-equivalent:
   for our own pid the self-clock is the same quantity ps-lstart would report,
   and the lock's `startRef` was written from it. Foreign-pid verification is
   unchanged and still fails closed when the probe is denied (ps on darwin,
   `/proc` fallback on linux).

2. **Quota custody — Linux fail-closed + own-custody coverage**
   `test/resource-quota-refresh-lease.test.ts` (which already mocks
   `readNativeBootIdentity: () => null`, simulating a non-darwin host):
   - new positive test: `lease.identity()` verifies own custody from the
     process start clock without a native probe.
   - new `it.each([2,3,4,5])`: a staged custody-bound pending marker on a
     host with no boot identity refuses acquisition with
     `reconciliation-required` / `boot-identity-unavailable` and preserves the
     marker — the Linux fail-closed custody path.

3. **Volume polling — real storage checker on the actual host**
   `test/resource-volume-polling.test.ts`: new darwin-gated test that swaps the
   mocked `execFileSync` for the real implementation and runs the full bounded
   sysctl/df/diskutil/plutil chain (`prepareResourceNativeProfile` →
   `resolveNativeSeatLaunch` fresh read → `resolveNativeSeatDisplayMetadata`
   cached read) against the actual host volume. On hosts where the bounded
   reads complete, it asserts the full positive path; where they cannot, it
   asserts documented fail-closed refusal — never a guessed identity.
   File added to `REAL_IO_TEST_FILES` (test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs):
   it now performs real I/O and belongs in the serialized real-io lane.

4. **Staging-stop — assert both settled and unattempted reports**
   `test/fleet-staging-batch-stop-05sta2.test.ts`: `--json` assertion now
   checks the settled `/fake/a` report AND the `/fake/b`
   `{complete: false, source: 'unattempted'}` report; `--text` assertion now
   checks the `skipped (unattempted)` line. Production already emitted both —
   the old assertion was stale.

## Dropped / stale

- **No production changes for staging-stop**: the unattempted report emission
  already exists on current HEAD (`fleet-staging-inventory-batch.ts`); only the
  stale assertion needed updating.
- **Boot-identity fail-closed**: already covered by
  `test/resource-native-boot-identity.test.ts` ("does not launch commands on
  unsupported platform linux/win32/freebsd") — not re-added.
- **Linux `/proc` foreign-pid fallback**: already implemented in
  `verifiedProcessStartIdentity` and covered by `m416.local-store-lock-handoff`
  — not re-added.

## Environment limitation (not a regression)

`/bin/ps` is denied by this host's sandbox (`bash: /bin/ps: Operation not
permitted`). The own-pid custody fix makes own-lease verification work anyway;
the two `resource-quota-native-lifecycle` real-io tests now advance past the
lease stage but still cannot complete here because the durable launch proof
requires `/bin/ps` inside the spawned launcher child (by design — signed
kernel child identity). They are expected to pass on hosts permitting ps.
Similarly `resource-quota-launch-handoff` (15) and one
`resource-quota-shared-evidence` test require foreign/child kernel probes and
remain environment-blocked. `diskutil` also ran ~1.1–1.5s on this loaded host
(fixed 1s spawn bound), so the real-host volume test exercised the fail-closed
branch here.

## Commands run

```
HOME=$(mktemp -d) ASHLR_HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run <focused files>
node scripts/verify-changed.mjs --force  # foreground — all PASS on final tree
node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit           # PASS (exit 0)

```

- fleet-staging-batch-stop-05sta2: 7/7, fleet-staging-stop-roots-05stc2: 8/8,
  resource-volume-polling: 7/7, resource-quota-refresh-lease: 31/31,
  resource-quota-inspection: 26/26, resource-native-boot-identity: 17/17
- resource-quota-native-lifecycle: 0/2 environment-blocked (see above —
  they now advance through the lease custody stage and stop only at the
  launcher child's ps-lstart proof, which this sandbox denies).
Wider custody spot-check (8 files): 187 passed, 16 env-blocked fails
(launch-handoff + shared-evidence — all require `/bin/ps` for foreign/child
identity, unchanged by this diff; verified same failures without the diff).

Pre-fix baseline on this host: staging --json test failed;

body:

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-MERGEBATCH-1

## What

`phm fleet merge-batch [--input <file>|-] [--repo <owner/name>] [--root <abs>] [--json]`
— a read-only merge-batch planner for the merge treadmill (~180 open bridge
PRs invalidating each other as main moves hourly).

- `src/core/fleet/merge-batch.ts` (new, 540 LOC): pure planner, no I/O.
  Parses three real snapshot shapes — a raw `gh pr list --json` array
  (`number,title,headRefName,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,createdAt,updatedAt,files`),
  a merge-backlog read `{v:1, items}` and a `fleet.pr-hygiene.v1` report —
  carrying the envelope's own read state (`input.upstream`), then builds the
  file-overlap graph: connected components become batches.
  Disjoint (independent) batches merge in any order/concurrently; serial
  batches get an order that minimizes rebase events = members − max
  independent set (greedy min-degree MIS, ties keep wide diffs clean),
  clean wave FIFO first, rebase wave least-ready last. Per-batch
  `conflictRisk` (0..1, documented formula) + `reasons`, hot files (≥3
  fan-in), and a flattened `order`. Emits `fleet.merge-batch.v1`.
- `src/cli/fleet-merge-batch.ts` (new, 237 LOC): thin CLI. Input precedence
  `--input` → piped stdin → `<root>/fleet/open-prs.json`
  (ASHLR_RUNS_DIR/`--root`, default ~/.ashlr-runs). Bounded 32 MiB reads.
  No gh calls anywhere. Exit 0 plan, 1 no usable snapshot (`input.state`
  honest: missing/unreadable/too-large/malformed — or the envelope's own
  upstream read failed, `input.upstream`), 2 usage. Classifies
  `read` in the fleet verb catalog.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`: regenerated (gen-fleet-registry).
- `src/cli/completions.ts`: `merge-batch` added to the fleet verb list.
- `src/cli/fleet-usage.ts` (+4/−1): drive-by — declared the missing
  `const usage` the registry-help test requires; the pre-existing suite
  failure (`verb "usage" has non-empty help text`) now passes. Error text
  changed `usage:` → `Usage:`; exit codes unchanged.
- `test/fleet-pr-batching.test.ts` (new, 370 LOC, 31 tests): named to keep
  the basename free of Tier-1 test stems (`merge` is one; a `*-merge-*`
  name would need a generated `.github/CODEOWNERS` line this job may not
  add). Covers parser shapes, dedupe/unreadable, star/clique batching,
  clean-wave exclusion for conflicted/BEHIND/draft PRs, FIFO and
  readiness ordering, hot files, risk ordering, and the CLI input paths.
- `docs/FLEET-MERGE-BATCH.md` (new, 73 LOC), `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md` row,
  `docs/README.md` index link (absolute URL — source-only doc, same
  convention as other unpackaged guides).

## Design notes

- Min rebases = batch size − clean-wave size: every PR ordered after an
  overlapping neighbour rebases once against accumulated main, so an
  independent set merges clean and the rest rebase once each.
- A zero-file PR is an independent batch with `evidence: 'no-file-data'` —
  unmeasured overlap, never silently proven-disjoint. `conflicted`/
  `BEHIND`/draft PRs can never join the clean wave (`rebase:
  'already-required'`).
- Batches sort safest-first; disjoint batches may still merge concurrently —
  the flat `order` is the serial-safe sequence, not a claim one is needed.

Reconciled the two teammate-delivered iMessage patches (personal Codex dot)
against fleet PRs #4063 and #4059. Consolidated result is left **uncommitted**
in this worktree on `codex-bridge/RQ-SWE3-DOTPATCH-1`, HEAD `addfd8cb2`.

REWORKS_PR: 4063
REWORKS_PR: 4059

## Access limitation (important for closers)

`~/.ashlr-runs/imessage/patches/` is **unreadable from this job's sandbox** —
macOS denies the whole `~/.ashlr-runs` tree (`Operation not permitted` for
`ls`/`stat`/`cat`, `permission denied` for direct file reads; a scope grant for
the path did not lift the OS-level deny). `gh` is also unusable here (its
`~/.config/gh` config is denied). So `git apply --check --recount` could not be
run on the RAW diff files themselves.

Mitigation: both fleet PR heads were fetched as git refs
(`refs/pull/4063/head`, `refs/pull/4059/head`) and audited line-by-line
against the patch intents described in the job packet. The PR heads provably
contain both patches' fixes *and* all five described regression tests — see
dispositions below. If the RAW diffs carry hunks beyond the described intent,
they could not be observed here; diff the RAW files against this worktree on
the host to confirm parity.

## Per-patch disposition

### patch-6e573cd2d93a.RAW.diff — SHA256 VERIFIED — ADOPTED (already upstream in PR #4063 head)

Targets `src/core/fleet/agent-activity.ts` + tests: delayed
finish/publish/outcome from an OLD attempt must not advance a requeued job
before relaunch; the later queue/launch time is the attempt boundary.

PR #4063 head (`5d520f739`, commit subject literally "fix teammate-review
finding on PR #") already implements exactly this: per-attempt `boundary =
max(queue, launch ts)`; `finish` requires `ev.ts >= a.boundary` (agent-activity.ts
:257), `publish` requires `ev.ts >= a.boundary` when no finish is recorded
(:267), `outcome`/`task_outcome` require `ev.ts >= a.boundary` (:277); a new
queue/launch after a terminal event starts a fresh attempt (`reset`, :242/:248).
All 3 described regression tests exist verbatim in `test/fleet-activity.test.ts`
(delayed finish :141, delayed publish :154, delayed outcome :120 — plus a 4th,
"stale outcome vs re-launched job" :106).

Audit for missed cases: a straggler stamped *after* the current boundary is
inherently indistinguishable by timestamp; the next queue/launch row
self-heals via `reset()` (`terminal && ev.ts >= lastBoundary`). Nothing in the
described intent remained uncovered — no extra hunks to port.

**Consolidated:** the full PR #4063 file set is ported onto this worktree's
main (module + thin CLI + `GET /api/fleet/activity` + docs + tests). The one
drifted file, `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`, was regenerated with
`node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs` so main's added loaders
(`precheck-repeats`, `sticky-loop`) and the new `activity` loader coexist.

### patch-200f7f9a7eaf.RAW.diff — hash UNVERIFIED — ADOPTED (superseded-equivalent in PR #4059 head)

Targets `src/core/comms/imessage-findings-bridge.ts` +
`test/imessage-findings-bridge.test.ts`: skip expired findings while advancing
the watermark; `readTeammateTexts({sinceMs})` takes an AGE DURATION — pass TTL,
not `now - TTL`.

PR #4059 head (`411b6aef7`) implements an **equal-or-stronger** version of both
fixes:

- Instead of passing `sinceMs: CHANNEL_BUS_TTL_MS` (the literal patch fix),
  the bridge reads the inbox **unbounded** (no `sinceMs`,
  imessage-findings-bridge.ts :152-154) — passing any duration would hide
  expired rows from the pass, so the rowid watermark could never advance past
  them. Expired rows are still refused inside the pass
  (`nowMs - Date.parse(row.at) > CHANNEL_BUS_TTL_MS`, :168) because an append
  would stamp a fresh 7-day TTL and revive them.
- Refused rows (expired, unbridgeable, store-terminal) are counted and advance
  `handled`/the watermark; transient store states break without advancing
  (:163-184). Doc comment :134-141 states the `sinceMs` age-duration semantics
  verbatim.

Both described regression tests exist verbatim: "never revives an expired
finding" (:152) and "advances the watermark past expired rows" (:161).

Audit: `isTextRow` (imessage-teammate-inbox.ts :62) guarantees parseable `at`,
so the `Date.parse` NaN edge in the expiry check is unreachable. Other
`readTeammateTexts` callers already pass durations correctly. Nothing missed.

**Consolidated:** the full PR #4059 file set is ported: findings bridge +
`imessage-inbox-bridge.ts` mirror hook (best effort; never changes receipts,
cursor or `ok`) + `imessage.ts` poll-line summary + docs (AGENT-BUS,
IMESSAGE) + the new suite and the teammate-ingest mirror assertions.

## Tier-1 closure growth (reviewed, regenerated per repo procedure)

The two new modules join the Tier-1 authority import closure:
`imessage-findings-bridge.ts` via the inbox-bridge mirror import, and
`agent-activity.ts` via `api.ts`'s literal dynamic `import()` (the `*-api.ts`
root exclusion does not stop members inside api.ts joining). Both are
read/report-only modules that change no gate decisions. Regenerated
`test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json` (+2 entries only) with
`ASHLR_UPDATE_TIER1_CLOSURE=1` — the same procedure prior bridge jobs used

review is still enforced at merge. New test files are not Tier-1 (no stem or

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-TOCTOU-RACE-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-TOCTOU-RACE-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `5344526f3`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-TOCTOU-RACE-1

Security follow-up to merged PR #4002 (RQ-SWE3-SEC-PATHS-1). Closes the
remaining intermediate-symlink TOCTOU in `readUnmetDeps`/`readDepPrompt`
(src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts) and hardens the two test gaps the job
named.

## What changed

### src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts (+54 / −6 net)

`readDepPrompt` previously proved containment with name-based checks that each
re-walked the mutable namespace: `open(resolved, O_NOFOLLOW)` → `realpath(resolved)`
→ `lstat(resolved)` dev/ino match. An attacker flipping an intermediate
symlink outside-for-open / inside-for-realpath / outside-for-lstat satisfied
every check while the descriptor read an outside file's DEPENDENCY GATE.

Containment is now proven against the held descriptor:

- `descriptorPath()` returns `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` on Linux/Android — realpath
  of an fd path is kernel truth about the pinned inode; a resolved answer that
  sits outside the root rejects outright.
- Portable POSIX bind: re-`open()` the **canonical** spelling
  (`realpath(resolved)` output carries no symlinks, so the flip cannot steer
  this second resolution) and require `dev`/`ino` equality with the opened fd.
  The flip can steer `open()` or `realpath()` but cannot make the canonical
  name resolve to the same outside inode — verified deterministically below.
- Post-read fence: `lstat(resolved)` identity must still match the fd and
  `realpath(resolved)` must be unchanged, so observed namespace churn
  discards the bytes (fail closed, matches the tree's documented
  changed-during-read doctrine).
- `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_NONBLOCK` now follow the repo's `typeof === 'number'` guard
  idiom (stable-file-read.ts) instead of bare constants.

Documented residual (unchanged, acknowledged in-tree elsewhere): Node has no
portable openat(2)/F_GETPATH, so a same-user attacker renaming *real*
directories can still race probes — the before/after checks make those swaps
observable and fail closed.

### test/fleet-runs-parked-unmet-deps.test.ts (+79 / −5 net)

- Deterministic race regression test: `vi.mock('node:fs/promises')` retargets
  `runs/queue/link` to outside for `open()`/`lstat()` and inside for
  `realpath()` at exactly the syscalls the exploit needed — no timing. Verified
  it fails on the pre-fix code (emitted `RQ-LEAK`) and passes on the fix.
- Oversized-file test now has read-byte assertions: `RQ-IN` ends inside the
  64 KiB window, `RQ-TAIL` sits wholly past it — the former unbounded
  `readFile` would have surfaced `RQ-TAIL`.
- All existing tests untouched in intent; mock is inert unless `raceCtl.active`.

## Verification (all with temporary HOME, hermetic)

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (foreground, once) | PASS — file selection, `tsc --noEmit`, realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe `8fa42ced97f9`. eslint skipped: `node_modules/eslint` absent in worktree (Merge Gate lints on CI) |
| `npm run check:docs` | PASS — 261 local links, 332 source links, 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run test/fleet-runs-parked-unmet-deps.test.ts` (+5 fleet files: parked-queue-oct31, parked-queue-repo-mix, parked-queue-next-up, fleet-status-api, fleet-live-queue-route-oct31) | PASS — 6 files, 29/29 tests |
| `npm run test:ci -- test/fleet-runs-parked-unmet-deps.test.ts` | PASS — 11/11 |
| Negative control: stash src fix, rerun suite | race test FAILS on old code (leaked `RQ-LEAK`), restored |

no `git commit`/`push`, no `gh` writes, `.github/` untouched.

hit `ETARGET` — the reconciled HTTP read and npm's own packument resolution can
sit on different registry replicas, so catalog readiness alone is insufficient.

This change adds a bounded retry for the no-scripts install/read path:

- `scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs`
  - `installPublishedArgs(version)` — the same command the consumer
    verification runs (`npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
    --save-exact --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org @ashlr/phantom@<v>`)
    plus `--prefer-online`, so each retry revalidates the packument over the
    network instead of replaying a locally cached (stale) response.
  - `installPublishedPackage(record, directory, deps)` — runs that install in a
    scratch consumer dir (creates a minimal private `package.json` if the
    caller did not `npm init` one), retries **ETARGET only** up to
    `INSTALL_ETARGET_ATTEMPTS = 4` total attempts with 5s/10s/20s backoff
    (~35s worst-case added latency), then holds. Every other failure — and any
    output mixing ETARGET with EINTEGRITY/EPROVENANCE/E401/E403/ENEEDAUTH —
    throws immediately with a bounded output tail. Nothing is suppressed and
    nothing is republished.
  - Post-install proof: `node_modules/@ashlr/phantom/package.json` name+version
    must equal the admitted record, and `node_modules/.package-lock.json`'s
    resolved `integrity` must equal `record.integrity` — a substituted or
    downgraded tree holds (stronger than the workflow's version-only check).
  - New CLI verb: `canonical-npm-publisher.mjs install <admittedDir>
    <consumerDir>` — verifies the handoff hashes exactly like the sibling
    verbs, then performs the bounded-retry install.
- `test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts` — new `no-scripts consumer install`
  describe (14 tests): exact argv, manifest creation/preservation, ETARGET
  retry+backoff+logging, bounded exhaustion, no-retry on
  integrity/provenance/auth/mixed/other failures, and version/integrity
  post-install holds.

## Required paired wiring (Security-owned `.github/` — NOT done here)

`.github/**` is `@masonwyatt23`-owned and this job's hard rules forbid editing
it, so the two bare `npm install` call sites need a paired pin that swaps them
for the new verb:

- `publish` job, step `Verify publisher provenance without executing candidate
  code` — replace the `npm init --yes` + `npm install --ignore-scripts ...
  "@ashlr/phantom@$VERSION"` + `test "$(node -p ...)" = "$VERSION"` lines with:

  ```bash
  mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer"
  node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs" install \
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-npm-admitted" "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer"
  ```

  (keep the following `cd`, `npm audit signatures`, and `provenance` lines).

- `consumer` job, step `Verify isolated public installed CLI` — replace the
  `env -i ... npm install --ignore-scripts ... "@ashlr/phantom@$VERSION"` line
  with:

  ```bash
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-home" \
    NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG="$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-npmrc" \
    node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs" install \
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-npm-admitted" "$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer"
  ```

  (keep the `ashlr --version` assertion; note it must then run from
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer`, or point at
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-consumer/node_modules/@ashlr/phantom/bin/ashlr`).

Until that pin lands the workflow behavior is unchanged; the verb is exercised
by the new tests and a stubbed-npm e2e below.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts` —
  **71/71 passed** (14 new).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (file selection,
  tsc --noEmit, realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe). eslint SKIP:
  `node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js` absent in this worktree; Merge Gate lints on
  CI. WARN: two pre-existing unrelated unchanged-file lane-lint notes.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` — errors: `[]`.
- `node --check scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs` — syntax OK.
- Manual e2e with a stubbed `npm` on PATH: 2×ETARGET (real 5s/10s backoff) then
  success — `exit=0`, installed tree + auto manifest verified; permanent
  ETARGET exhausted at 4 attempts and threw with the npm output tail.
- No git/gh writes; `.github/` untouched; hermetic tests only (tmpdir +
  injected exec/sleep; no real HOME, registry, or credentials).

## Net LOC

`+194 / -2` — `scripts/canonical-npm-publisher.mjs` +82,
`test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts` +112/−2. Two files changed.

## Notes for the closer

- The same-runner build+smoke path (RQ-CI-SAME-RUNNER-SMOKE-NOV7) is untouched;
  this diff is additive inside the publisher script and its test.
- `--prefer-online` is the only flag added to the install argv vs. the current
  workflow lines; it makes retries meaningful (forces packument revalidation)
  and is read-only.
- The retry never calls `npm publish`, never touches dist-tags, and does not
  catch or downgrade assertion failures — it fails the step loudly after
  `INSTALL_ETARGET_ATTEMPTS`.
</details>

## Summary

Deep web research on open-source agent-to-agent communication and
orchestration/subagent projects for Phantom's fleet. Produced
`docs/research/RQ-OSS-A2A-ORCH-1.md` with a 26-row ranked adoption table

libraries), a concrete Phantom gap analysis, four proposed READY
implementation one-liners, limitations, and full sources. Added an index
bullet in `docs/research/README.md`. No code changes — research artifact
only, per the job spec.

- **Adopt**: A2A object-model alignment for the unimplemented bus v2 contract
  (Apache-2.0, Linux Foundation); a Hatchet-vs-DBOS spike (both MIT,
  Postgres-backed) for durable cross-host job handoff to the hosted box.
- **License traps caught by verification**: Inngest is SSPL-1.0, Restate is
  BUSL-1.1, multica is a modified Apache-2.0 with commercial conditions —
  all source-available, never adopt. AutoGen root LICENSE is CC-BY-4.0 (code
  MIT in `LICENSE-CODE`); Mastra has `ee/` dirs under a separate license.

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-STAGINGSCANBUDGET05SSU2
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-STAGINGSCANBUDGET05SSU2` (pool: claude-api), single commit on base `7db1e2a91`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-STAGINGSCANBUDGET05SSU2 bridge notes

## Summary

`fleet staging-inventory` now runs under a finite total wall-time budget.
Previously it scanned up to 200 children sequentially, each `du` with a 30 s
timeout and no aggregate deadline. Now:

- **Budget:** `--max-duration-ms <integer>` sets a total budget that starts before
  listing. Default `120000` ms, valid range 1 to `3600000`. `--help` documents both.
- **Per-du cap:** before each measurement the remaining budget is computed.
  The du timeout is `min(30000, floor(remaining))`. A remainder below 1 ms counts as
  exhausted, because `execFileSync` treats `timeout: 0` as no timeout.
- **Exhaustion:** once the budget is spent, no further `du` starts. Remaining
  children are listed with `bytes: null` and `measurement: "not-attempted"`.
  The report sets `complete: false` and `incompleteReasons` includes
  `budget-exhausted`.
- **Honest counts:** `measurements` gives `measured`, `unmeasured`, `failed`
  and `notAttempted`. `totalMeasuredBytes` sums measured entries only. Human
  output adds `Total excludes N unmeasured entries; it is a lower bound.`
- **Distinct reasons:** `incompleteReasons` takes values `listing-degraded`,
  `truncated`, `budget-exhausted` and `measurement-failed`. A du timeout or
  failure yields `measurement-failed`, not exhaustion.
- **Seams:** `InventoryDeps.clock` is an injectable monotonic clock (default
  `performance.now()`). `measure(path, timeoutMs)` is the du runner and now

# BRIDGE_NOTES: ci-receipt-retry-batch (RQ-PHX-CIRECEIPTRETRY05SSH1)

## Summary

Implemented `ci-receipt-retry-batch` — a retry verb for the Ashlr fleet CLI that selects failed and not-started entries from a previous `ci-receipt-await-batch` report and passes them once to `awaitCiReceiptBatch` under a fresh shared deadline.

## Files changed

| Path | Type | Lines |
|------|------|-------|
| `src/core/fleet/ci-receipt-retry-batch.ts` | NEW | 183 |
| `src/cli/fleet-ci-receipt-retry-batch.ts` | NEW | 123 |
| `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` | MODIFIED | +1 (auto-regenerated) |
| `test/fleet-ci-receipt-retry-batch-05ssh1.test.ts` | NEW | 448 |
| **Implementation total** | | **306** |
| **Test total** | | **448** |

## Behavior

### Command
```
ashlr fleet ci-receipt-retry-batch --stdin --timeout-ms N [--poll-ms N] [--json]
```

### Input
Stdin must be a version-1 batch report (max 64 KiB UTF-8 JSON):
```json
{"version":1,"total":N,"bound":N,"failed":N,"notStarted":N,"timedOut":bool,"aborted":bool,"entries":[...]}
```

### Processing
1. Entire document validated before any network touch
2. Unknown keys, malformed counts, duplicate identities, or out-of-range retry counts rejected (exit 2)
3. Failed and not-started entries extracted in original order
4. Bound entries silently skipped — zero network reads
5. Retry targets deduplicated by exact identity (case-insensitive on repo)
6. Delegate once to `awaitCiReceiptBatch` with a fresh shared deadline
7. When no unresolved targets remain, emit an empty successful report (no waiter called)

### Output
Same batch report schema as `ci-receipt-await-batch` — the retry batch report. Pipeable for a second retry.

### Exit codes
- **0**: All bound or no unresolved targets (empty report)
- **1**: Any unresolved target failed or not-started
- **2**: Invalid input

```sh
node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs

# Run tests (hermetic, temp HOME)

# TypeScript check (tsc silent — no errors)
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
```

## Summary

Optional per-target wait bound for `fleet ci-receipt-await-batch` (Mason Nov 5
01:47 RESUME-FROM-FAILURE / t1626u batching orders). A recovery operator can
give each receipt target a bounded share of the batch wait so one still-running

network read in flight.

- `src/core/fleet/ci-receipt-await-batch.ts`: new `targetTimeoutMs?: number` on

  `min(targetTimeoutMs, remaining shared deadline)` — never more, so no local
  allowance can enlarge the global deadline. A target that exhausts its local
  share is a normal `failed` entry (sanitized reason, `prior: null` — no
  fabricated evidence); the next target starts only while shared time remains.
  Omitted option preserves the existing behavior exactly (`timeoutMs:
  remaining`).

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PHX-CIPLANAWAIT05SRW1

## Summary

`ashlr fleet ci-resume-plan` now has two mutually exclusive ways to obtain receipts:

- `--artifact-id ID [--archive file.zip]`: unchanged behavior, calls `fetchCiResumeReceipts`.
- `--artifact-name NAME --await-ms N [--poll-ms N]`: calls `awaitCiReceipt`, which polls the exact run/attempt with bounded GETs, then binds the named artifact through `discoverCiReceiptPrior` and the existing receipt binder.

Both modes feed the same prior-repo check and `planCiResumeInputs`, so the plan is the same for the same evidence. The manifest is read and parsed before any wait or remote call. `--archive` is valid only with `--artifact-id`.

Invalid combinations exit 2 before remote work: both or neither acquisition mode, `--artifact-name` without `--await-ms`, `--archive` with the name mode, `--await-ms`/`--poll-ms` with the id mode, duplicate flags, and out-of-bound or non-numeric values (`--await-ms` in 1..3600000, `--poll-ms` in 250..3600000, default 5000).

A terminal missing artifact, abort or timeout returns exit 1 with empty stdout and no plan. Diagnostics stay on stderr and stdout carries one plan JSON document.

The new optional deps seam is `FleetCiResumePlanDeps { now?, sleep?, signal? }`, passed through to `awaitCiReceipt`. Production defaults (`performance.now`, `abortableSleep`) are used when omitted.

## Changed paths

- `src/cli/fleet-ci-resume-plan.ts` (modified): mode parsing (`acquisition()`), await branch, deps seam, updated usage line.
- `test/fleet-ci-resume-plan-await-05srw1.test.ts` (new): 7 tests.

No other files were edited. No `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `src/cli/fleet.ts`, registry/index/help/completions, manifests, pinned tooling, or release scripts were touched. Nothing is committed.

   Result: 2 files passed, 11 tests passed, 0 failed. That is 7 new await-mode tests and the 4 existing artifact-id tests.
3. `npx eslint src/cli/fleet-ci-resume-plan.ts` then `npx eslint test/fleet-ci-resume-plan-await-05srw1.test.ts`, run sequentially: both exit 0.
   First attempt failed with `Cannot find module '../lib/cli'` because `node_modules/eslint` was a partial copy with no `lib/`. Repaired by running `npm run install:worktree` (pnpm 10.28.2 frozen install, `--ignore-scripts`, store under the shared git common dir). It exited 0. ESLint then ran cleanly.

Tracked files: `src/cli/fleet-ci-resume-plan.ts` +56 / -8. New test file +244. Total +300 / -8 (net +292). BRIDGE_NOTES.md adds about 60 lines.

## Test design notes

- The real await, discovery, binder and planner run. Only `gh` is faked, and `run download` writes receipts.json into the requested `--dir`.
- Virtual time: `sleep` advances a fake clock and records the sleep durations. The pending test asserts exactly two sleeps of 500 ms. The timeout test asserts four sleeps of 250 ms and no download.

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-MCPEMAILBATCH05SRD1

## Summary

Adds `fleet_email_outbox_batch_await` to the isolated fleet MCP server so a
Comms MCP session can await up to 50 reply artifacts in one bounded call
(serving t1618u Comms handoff, t1613u tool parity, t1626u related-task
batching). It reuses the already-merged `awaitEmailOutboxBatch` core waiter —
no second poller — and mirrors the single-artifact `fleet_email_outbox_await`
adapter for config resolution, sourceState honesty, cancellation and output
shape.

## Files changed (396 insertions, 2 deletions)

- `src/mcp/fleet-email-outbox-batch-await.ts` (new, 109 lines): args type
  (`names` 1..50 distinct safe `.reply.eml` basenames, `timeoutMs` 1..300000,
  optional `pollMs` 100..10000), `parseFleetEmailOutboxBatchAwaitArgs`
  (rejects unknown keys and path-bearing names exactly like the CLI), and
  `readFleetEmailOutboxBatchAwait` (resolves the saved email-drop config at
  the server-owned runs dir with the `outboxDir` → `inboxDir`-sibling
  fallback; stat-probes the outbox; delegates to `awaitEmailOutboxBatch` with
  the MCP request `AbortSignal`). Report: `schemaVersion: 1`,
  `snapshotKind: 'local-persisted'`, `authority: 'none'`, `generatedAt`,
  `sourceState` (`ok | missing-config | invalid-config | missing-outbox |
  unreadable-outbox | unobserved`), `rows` (per-name state + fixed stuck
  reason, null whenever the source failed so a broken source never reads as
  an empty batch), `timedOut`, `cancelled`, `sourceFailure`. Deps seams:
  `runsDir`, `readConfig`, `awaitBatch`.
- `src/mcp/fleet-server.ts` (+27/-1): import, `FleetReaders.
  emailOutboxBatchAwait` seam, tools/list entry with read-only annotations
  and a strict JSON schema, allowlist/parse/validation/dispatch wiring, and
  `extra.signal` passed to the reader.
- `test/mcp/fleet-email-outbox-batch-await-05srd1.test.ts` (new, 260 lines):
  real `createFleetServer` + real `Client` over `InMemoryTransport`.
- `test/mcp/fleet-server.test.ts` (+1/-1): pinned tool-name list updated for
  the new tool — required to keep the existing listing assertion green (same
  pattern as the sibling single-await job, commit 9a433a27f).

## Behavior guarantees

- Cancellation before config read or between config read and polling returns
  `sourceState: 'unobserved'`, `cancelled: true` without touching the
  filesystem; mid-wait abort surfaces through the shared `AbortSignal` into
  the batch waiter (`cancelled: true`).
- Missing/invalid config, missing/unreadable outbox and mid-poll source
  loss all return `sourceFailure: true` with `rows: null`; a `drafted` row
  means drafted (never sent/delivered); no send action, bodies, recipients,
  credentials or config contents are ever emitted.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/mcp/fleet-email-outbox-batch-await-05srd1.test.ts` — **39/39 pass**

title: bridge: RQ-FIXUP-CI-ONBOARD-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-FIXUP-CI-ONBOARD-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `767470344`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** src/core/resources/worker-bindings.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-FIXUP-CI-ONBOARD-1

## Summary

Two distinct regressions kept the master onboarding tests red on the daily
full-suite lane (CI run 41873017470, sha d6a2c5f96c33d0ac60b63ada7222cf5a50a3f2b6).

### 1. `test/onboard-detect.test.ts` — `TypeError: saveAutomation is not a function` (3 tests)

The test imports `saveAutomation` from the `src/core/automations/index.ts`
barrel, but the barrel imported it only for internal use and never re-exported
it. Added `saveAutomation` to the store re-export line. The test predates both
regressions (present since bootstrap commit 84080b77c) and is not stale, so the
source barrel was fixed.

### 2. `test/m20.onboard.test.ts` — `Test timed out in 5000ms`

Root cause was twofold:

a. **Never-settling child-process Promises** under the test's black-holed
   `node:child_process` mocks (mocks record calls but never invoke callbacks or
   emit events):
   - `src/core/tools-registry.ts` `runProbeAsync` awaited an `execFile` callback
     that can never fire when `execFile` returns no child handle. A spawn that
     yields no child can't be awaited — the probe now resolves instead of
     parking the whole tools registry forever.
   - `src/core/run/verify-commands.ts` `runVerifySubprocessAsync` could only
     settle via its ~5s timeout, and its cleanup crashed on child handles
     lacking `kill`/`unref`/`removeAllListeners`. A child the runner cannot
     signal or observe cannot be bounded by its deadlines, so it now fails
     closed as a spawn failure (`'spawn returned a process handle without
     termination authority'`) instead of awaiting a ghost.
   These map to upstream regressions: PR #1555 (9b777776da, Oct 31) switched
   doctor's tools probe to the async `{parallel:true}` path, and PR #1042
   (7fe729948a, Oct 28) added the pool CLI check that reaches the bounded
   runner. The m20 test (Oct 16) predates both. Daily full-suite CI has been
   red since Oct 27, consistent with that window.

b. **A ~600-module eager import graph**: `onboard.ts` → `doctor.ts` →
   `pool-cli-doctor.ts` → `worker`/`pool-cli-versions` → `verify-commands` →
   `mcp-native` pulled essentially the whole app, so the first test's 5s window
   paid the full transform cost. `onboard.ts`'s static closure is now 43
   modules:
   - onboard.ts: extended-surface deps (`daemon/service*`, `engine-readiness`,
     `sandbox/policy`, `frontier-usage`, `index-engine`, `readiness`,
     `integrations/secrets`) load inside their step functions; `onboard()`
     itself only loads its eight-step path.
   - doctor.ts: `checkPoolCliVersions`, provider registry, receipt store and
     the worktree reaper moved into runDoctor's existing parallel prefetch
     wave (matching the file's `try*` convention), and `prewarmDoctor()` lets
     `onboard()` overlap that load with its earlier steps.
   - `renderToolText`/`textResult`/`NativeToolResult`/caps moved beside the
     strict `scrubSecrets` in `knowledge/index.ts` (re-exported from
     `mcp-native.ts`, so every existing import surface is unchanged) —
     `verify-commands.ts` no longer imports the 584-module `mcp-native` hub.
   - `workerEnvironment` moved to the pure `worker-bindings.ts` module
     (re-exported from `worker.ts`), so light probes don't load the worker
     dispatch graph.
   - `pool-cli-versions.ts` lazy-loads the bounded runner per probe;
     `pool-cli-doctor.ts` lazy-loads everything except its own code and reads
     the roster file only when it exists (skipping the `pool-runtime` universe
     entirely when there is no `connections.json`).
   - All lazy-import targets are existing Tier-1 closure members; no new files
     were created and `tier1-closure.json`/CODEOWNERS/protected paths are
     untouched.

## Commands run

- `gh run view 41873017470 -R ashlrai/phantom --log-failed` — failed: the
  sandbox denied gh's config read (`operation not permitted` on
  `~/.config/gh/config.yml`). GitHub's unauthenticated REST API was used for
  run metadata, jobs and check-run annotations; no per-test log text was
  exposed by that API, so the failures were reproduced locally instead.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m20.onboard.test.ts --bail 1` — PASS
  33/33 (three consecutive runs).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/onboard-detect.test.ts` — PASS 10/10.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m20.onboard.test.ts test/onboard-detect.test.ts --bail 1`
  — see Pass/fail below.
- Scoped `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --strict --module nodenext` on all 11
  touched files — clean.
- `node scripts/check-realio-lane-membership.mjs` — ok (634 real-io, 2455
  unit, no unclassified markers).
- `node scripts/check-verse-sync-io.mjs` — ok.
- `npx eslint <files>` — could not run: the eslint install in this worktree is
  broken (`Cannot find module '../lib/cli'`). Scoped tsc plus the lane lints
  were used instead.
- esbuild/static-closure counters for import-graph measurement (scratch test
  files created during diagnosis were removed).

## Pass/fail

- Before: `onboard-detect` 7/10 (3 failures, `saveAutomation is not a
  function`); `m20` first `onboard()` test timed out at 5000ms and every
  `onboard()` call hung forever under the mocks (`--bail` masked the remaining
  32).
- After (this worktree):
  - `test/m20.onboard.test.ts`: 33/33 passed on every solo run.
  - `test/onboard-detect.test.ts`: 10/10 passed.
  - The exact combined command (`npx vitest run test/m20.onboard.test.ts
    test/onboard-detect.test.ts --bail 1`): on this heavily contended host
    (load avg 90-124; two workers each cold-transforming ~240 modules), the
    first m20 test measured 5012-5031ms and tipped over the 5000ms budget in
    some runs while passing in quieter windows (solo file total 4.79s). The
    deterministic defects — never-settling probes and the missing export —
    are fixed outright; remaining sensitivity is transform-cost variance on a
    saturated machine, not correctness. CI workers are far faster per module
    and ran this test green before the regressions landed.

## Net LOC

+215 / -92 = +123 across 11 files:

- src/core/automations/index.ts (+1/-1)
- src/core/doctor.ts (+71/-12)
- src/core/knowledge/index.ts (+45/-0)
- src/core/mcp-native.ts (+22/-34)
- src/core/onboard.ts (+30/-12)
- src/core/resources/pool-cli-doctor.ts (+20/-7)
- src/core/resources/pool-cli-versions.ts (+3/-1)
- src/core/resources/worker-bindings.ts (+15/-0)
- src/core/resources/worker.ts (+3/-11)
- src/core/run/verify-commands.ts (+13/-1)
- src/core/tools-registry.ts (+4/-1)

## Behavior notes

- `checkWorktreeStorage` now takes its probe as a required parameter;
  `runDoctor` injects the lazily loaded probe, and every existing caller
  (tests) already injected one.
- `checkReceiptVerify` with no status probe reports 'receipt store
  unavailable' rather than reading the store itself; `runDoctor` injects the
  real probe and all test callers inject.
- A degraded `'pool-cli'` warn check is emitted when the pool-cli check module
  can't load, matching the file's other `try*` degradations.
- `runVerifySubprocessAsync` fails closed on a process handle it cannot
  signal/observe; previously such a child could only end via its timeout and
  cleanup could throw.
- `runProbeAsync` resolves `null` when `execFile` returns no child handle;
  previously it parked forever.
- `prewarmDoctor` runs no probes and mutates nothing; it only begins the same
  dynamic imports runDoctor performs.
- No test, budget, gate, or secret-shape control was loosened. No new CLI/API
  surface was added. Changes remain uncommitted.
</details>

  * Verification and probe commands handle missing or invalid process handles as failures rather than waiting indefinitely.

All 16 tests passed (192ms total):

1. ✓ Convention export + `--ids-stdin` in help text

4. ✓ Empty/malformed/oversize/duplicate/mixed input → exit 2

7. ✓ Oversized stdin (> 16 KiB) → exit 2, no echo

10. ✓ SIGTERM during stdin collection → exit 130, listener cleanup
11. ✓ Pre-aborted injected signal → exit 2

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-SELFTICKSTRAYSTOP03
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-SELFTICKSTRAYSTOP03` (pool: claude), single commit on base `a3991e6e9`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: self-tick stray-stop (RQ-PHX-SELFTICKSTRAYSTOP03)

## Behavior change
`fleet self-tick` now runs a `stray-stop` step after `lane-autohold` and before `planner-tick`, so slots freed from
finished-job strays count for the planner in the same pass. It is bound to `cmdFleetStrayStop` with the shared argv
plus `--max 5` (at most 5 processes signalled per tick). Dry-run stays a dry run (no `--apply`, no signals). The
verb's own safety checks are unchanged. There was no existing per-step kill-switch, so none was added.

- `src/core/fleet/self-tick.ts`: step name, order, header list. `stray-stop` is the only optional seam in `SelfTickSteps`; an unbound seam is skipped (no record), so older embedders keep working.
- `src/cli/fleet-self-tick.ts`: binding, usage text, human summary line. The verb prints with `console.log` and has no output seam, so the binding captures `console.log` for the step (steps run serially under the lock). A `strayStop` dep injects the reader/kill/ledger for tests.
- A caller that injects its own `steps` table owns the whole table; the real stray-stop joins only the default table (or when `strayStop` is passed). This keeps existing tests from reading the real process table.
- `self-tick-last.ts` needed no change: its step-name allow list derives from `SELF_TICK_STEP_ORDER`. No change to the web `self-tick-query.ts`.
- Existing tests touched only for exact step lists: `self-tick-inbox-acks-04`, `self-tick-order-notices-05`, `self-tick-landed-sweep-03`.
- New: `test/fleet-self-tick-stray-stop-03.test.ts`.

## Known caveat
On a host with no `~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/jobs.jsonl`, the real reader throws, `stray-stop` exits 1, and the tick records it `failed`. I left stray-slots.ts alone to stay inside the file budget.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run` on the self-tick, self-loop, stray-stop and doc-facts suites: 317 passed, 4 failed.
  - Pre-existing (fail on untouched origin/master too): `fleet-self-tick-api-02` (mount order), `fleet-self-tick-await-02sole2` (busy record), `doc-facts` (job-latency / repo-rate doc lines).
  - One further timing-sensitive failure (`final-summary format`) passed on rerun.
  - New test file and the three edited tests pass.
- `npx eslint` could not run: this checkout's `node_modules/eslint` is broken (`Cannot find module '../lib/cli'`). Lint is NOT verified.
- tsgo is not installed (npx 404); used `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: exit 0, no output.
- Branch fast-forwarded to origin/master; `git diff --stat origin/master`: 5 tracked files changed + 1 new test file.
- Net LOC: about +55/-16 tracked, plus about 110 new test lines.
</details>

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

  * Self-tick can now stop up to five processes reported as holding finished lane slots.
  * Added advisory resource waste-risk projections and desktop notifications when a lane enters high risk near reset.
* **Documentation**
  * Expanded guidance for fleet reports, resource risk, and the Z.ai coding lane.
  * Updated help text, wiring status documentation, and documentation links.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PHX-APPSPROBESCOPE03SONQ1

## Behavior

Added repeatable `--app` support to the fleet apps-status and fleet-apps-changes CLI paths, closing the gap between the MCP API (which already accepts `?app=` selection) and the CLI child-path.

### `fleet apps-status` — new `--app <name>` flag
- **Validation**: Unknown app names are rejected (exit 2) before `locateScript` or `execFile` are invoked. Duplicate `--app` flags are rejected as duplicates. Missing values or values starting with `-` are rejected. Only allowlisted names from `FLEET_APPS` are accepted.
- **Deduplication**: Duplicate selections are collapsed via a `Set<string>`. Canonical catalog order is enforced in the output.
- **Filtering**: When `--app` is provided, only the selected apps appear in the JSON output and the CLI print output. The internal `readFleetAppsStatus` still probes all apps (for degraded availability computation), but the CLI output is filtered to selected rows.
- **Default**: When no `--app` is given, the command retains full inventory behavior (all 8 apps).
- **Help text**: Updated to document `[--app <name>]...`.

### `fleet apps-changes` — selection forwarding
- The `observeFleetAppsChanges` function now forwards the `--app` selection as CLI arguments to each `apps-status` child call via `runChild`.

# BRIDGE NOTES: RQ-PHX-STANDBYAPIEXEC02SOMI1

## Summary
Fixed the fleet-standby API to correctly invoke `scripts/mac-bridge/standby_readiness.py`.
The API was passing `-I` (isolated mode, which strips the script's directory from `sys.path`) and
`--json` (not supported by the Python parser). Also fixed a logic bug where `available` was
hardcoded to `true` regardless of the Python report.

## Exact Changes

### 1. `src/core/verse/fleet-standby-api.ts` (3 lines changed)
- **`-I` → `-B`**: The `-B` flag (no `.pyc`) preserves `sys.path[0]` as the script's directory,
  allowing the Python script to import sibling modules (`host_lease`, `latest_failover`, etc.).
  `-I` (isolated mode) strips this, causing `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- **Removed `argv.push('--json')`**: The Python `build_parser()` has no `--json` flag;
  the script always outputs JSON, so the flag is unnecessary and causes `argparse` errors.
- **`available: true` → `available: report.ready`**: The API was unconditionally setting
  `available: true` on validation pass. Now it correctly reflects `report.ready` from the
  Python script. When the Python report has blockers (`ready: false`), `available` is `false`.

### 2. `test/verse-fleet-standby-api.test.ts` (1 line changed)
- Updated expected `exec` argv from `-I` to `-B`, removed `--json` from expected argv.

### 3. `test/standby-api-real-python-02somi1.test.ts` (new, 168 lines)
- **Real Python invocation tests** (not mocking `exec`):
  - `real python3 argv/import fix: fake lease + no snapshot`: Creates a valid lease DB,
    empty snapshot store, and proves the Python script returns `no-snapshot` blocker,
    yielding `configured: true, available: false, blocker: 'no-snapshot'`.
  - `real python3 returns blocker no-lease-db when DB is absent`: Missing DB path
    produces `blocker: 'no-lease-db'`.
  - `cache coalescing works with real python3 invocation`: Verifies concurrent API calls
    within the 30s cache window coalesce to a single Python invocation.
- All tests use `python3 -B` with a bounded explicit argv (no shell, no PYTHONPATH).

## Commands Run
```

python3 -I scripts/mac-bridge/standby_readiness.py --db x --snapshot-store y \
  --primary p --role r --host h  # → ModuleNotFoundError

# Verify the fix: -B preserves sys.path for imports
cd scripts/mac-bridge && python3 -B standby_readiness.py --db x ...  # → ModuleNotFoundError
  (still fails from wrong dir; correct when in scripts/mac-bridge/)

# Test suites
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/verse-fleet-standby-api.test.ts      # 10 tests passed
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/standby-api-real-python-02somi1.test.ts  # 3 tests passed
```

- TypeScript typecheck: passed

Loopback-only eval bench for candidate local models (default `lfm3:1.7b`,
`d1:2b`) against the incumbent local tier (`DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL_TAG` =

title: bridge: RQ-MERGEFLOWNOV1Q8
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-MERGEFLOWNOV1Q8` (pool: devin), single commit on base `85c49a2d9`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** src/cli/autopilot.ts src/core/autopilot/act.ts src/core/autopilot/diagnose.ts src/core/autopilot/github.ts test/autopilot.test.ts

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE NOTES — RQ-MERGEFLOWNOV1Q8

## Task

Inspect the existing merge queue controller and its tests; automatically recut
conflicting PRs against current main and requeue them after required checks
pass. Add tests for conflict recovery, idempotent retries, and preserving
required checks.

## Component

The merge queue controller is the PR autopilot (`src/core/autopilot/`,
`phm autopilot [--all|--watch]`). It already owned the conflict→recut path
(diagnose `plan` → `recut`; act pushes `<head>-recut` and opens a replacement
PR). The gap: a conflict ejects a lane from GitHub's merge queue, and the
recut replacement was never re-queued — the queue slot was silently lost.

## What changed

- `src/core/autopilot/diagnose.ts`
  - `PrView.autoMerge` (reads REST `auto_merge`): whether the PR holds a
    merge-queue slot.
  - `Observation.recut` extended with the requeue read: `headSha`,
    `mergeable`, `draft`, `autoMerge`, `requiredChecks`.
  - New `Plan` action `requeue` (`{ recut, headSha }`).
  - New pure `requiredCheckState(contexts, runs, statuses)` evaluator:
    'green' only when every required context's newest check run **and**
    commit status on the exact head passed; 'none' when protection names no
    required contexts or is unreadable (fail closed — a head nothing gates is
    never queued).
  - `plan()`: a live open recut is requeued only when it is mergeable, not a
    draft, not already queued, and `requiredChecks === 'green'`. Pending or
    red required checks, an unreadable protection read, a fresh conflict, or
    two already-refused queue calls at that head all wait — the original PR
    is never closed before the recut merges (unchanged invariant).
- `src/core/autopilot/github.ts`
  - `readPr` parses `auto_merge`.
  - `readStatuses` — newest commit status per context (required contexts can
    report via statuses, not only check runs; same convention as
    `fleet/host-merge.ts`).
  - `readRequiredContexts` — required context names from ruleset
    `required_status_checks` rules ∪ classic branch protection
    (`enforcement_level === 'off'` ignored). `null` when neither source
    could be read → gate waits.
  - `queueMerge` — `gh pr merge <n> --repo <repo> --squash --auto
    --match-head-commit <headSha>` — the same queueing `improve promote
    --queue-merge` uses (auto-merge has no REST endpoint; the pin refuses a
    moved head). Queueing only — branch protection and required checks still
    decide the merge; the autopilot itself never merges.
- `src/core/autopilot/act.ts`
  - `readRecut` reads the full replacement PR plus its required-check state
    (skipped once it is already queued — GitHub's own `auto_merge` is the
    idempotency marker).
  - `tick()` handles `requeue`: KILL/pause re-read, the `requeue:<head>`
    attempt is counted and saved *before* the call (a crash/refusal can never
    burst; at most two tries per head), result `'requeued'`.
- `src/cli/autopilot.ts`, `docs/cli.md` — wording only.

## Tests added (test/autopilot.test.ts, 38 total)

- Plan level: requeue fires only on verified-green head; waits on pending /
  red / none / unread required checks, draft, `mergeable` null/false,
  already-queued, branch-only recut; two refused calls stop retrying.
- `requiredCheckState` unit cases incl. commit statuses and mixed
  run+status contexts.
- `readRequiredContexts` against a fake `gh`: rulesets ∪ classic,
  unreadable → null, empty → [], enforcement off → [].
- Tick level (real git, fake GitHub):
  - conflict → recut → wait while a required check is pending →
    `requeue`/`requeued` once required checks pass (incl. a status-reported
    context) → idempotent wait once queued → `close-superseded` still closes
    the original.
  - required check missing / red / draft → never queued.
  - refused queue calls → counted before asking, one retry, then wait for a
    person (no third call, nothing queued by accident).
  - no required contexts / protection unreadable → queues nothing.

## Commands run

- `npm ci` (node_modules was missing eslint's lib/ in this worktree)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/autopilot.test.ts` — **38/38 pass**
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts` — 4 pass, 2
  pre-existing failures (`docs/AGENT-OPERATIONS.md` references `phm top`;
  the src/ flag scan hit its 5s timeout)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/protected-paths-310b.test.ts
  test/improve-promote-redteam.test.ts` — 180 pass; 1 borderline-timeout
  flake in `standingMetricConfinement` (transform ~57s + 60s cap; passes
  on baseline, unrelated to this change)
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS file selection, PASS eslint
  changed files, PASS tsc --noEmit, web typecheck skipped, PASS verse
  sync-I/O lint; `realio lane lint` FAIL is **pre-existing** (stale
  KNOWN_FAST_SPAWN_FILES entries + unrelated files flagged; identical on a
  stashed baseline run). `test/autopilot.test.ts` is already in
  REAL_IO_TEST_FILES.
- `node_modules/.bin/eslint -- <changed files>` — clean (exit 0)
- `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` — clean (exit 0)
- `npm run check:docs` — errors: []

## Net LOC

`git diff --shortstat`: 6 files changed, +373 / -20 → **net +353**
(test/autopilot.test.ts +193/-13, core +166, cli +9/-1, docs/cli.md +1/-1).

## Known limits / notes

- Requeue is unconditional on verified-green recuts (per the task text);
  it only ever *queues* — required checks and branch protection still decide
  the merge (`--match-head-commit` pins the head; a moved head disables it).
- A repo with zero required contexts, or protection that cannot be read,
  never triggers a requeue — conservative by design.
- `readRequiredContexts` matches required checks by context name (same as
  `gh pr checks --required`); the fleet merge machinery's stricter
  app-id binding was deliberately not imported into the autopilot.
- No commits made; all changes left uncommitted in the worktree.
</details>
